metadata.name: Ecodesign for Julia
metadata.description: Ecodesign rules for Julia code: type stability, allocations under control, bounded threading.

perf.name: Julia — allocations and types
perf.description: Type instability and hidden allocations dominate the cost of a hot function (RGESN Algorithms).

rules.title: Global variable read from a hot function
rules.description: A non-constant global has no fixed type, so the compiler cannot specialise the function that reads it and boxes every value instead. The cost is paid on every call.
rules.recommendation: Pass the value as an argument, or declare it const when it genuinely never changes. Check with @code_warntype before optimising anything else.
rules.note: A top-level assignment is normal in a script and only costs inside a hot function. The pattern marks the place to run @code_warntype, not a defect.

rules.title: Array grown by push! in a loop
rules.description: Growing an array by repeated push! reallocates and copies as it doubles. When the final size is known, that work is entirely avoidable.
rules.recommendation: Preallocate with sizehint! or Vector{T}(undef, n) when the size is known, and mutate in place. Reuse the buffer across iterations.

example.bad:
r = []
for x in xs; push!(r, f(x)); end
example.good:
r = Vector{Float64}(undef, length(xs))
@inbounds for i in eachindex(xs); r[i] = f(xs[i]); end

rules.note: One sizehint! or one undef allocation anywhere in the file silences the rule. push! on a short, unknown-length collection is perfectly reasonable; the size is what settles it.

rules.title: Threading without a bound
rules.description: @threads over a large range takes every core the runtime was given, for a gain that depends on the work per item. On a shared machine it takes them from something else.
rules.recommendation: Measure the sequential version first, then size the parallelism to the work per item and to what the machine can spare. Compile and warm up before comparing steady-state timings.
